title: Portrait of the Great Barred Spiral
caption: The Great Barred Spiral Galaxy, NGC 1365, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope
credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Image processing: Travis Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), Jen Miller (Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab), Mahdi Zamani & Davide de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A prominent bar crosses the middle of NGC 1365, along with graceful spiral arms and lanes of dust dimming the broad, diffuse glow of stars. Also known as the Great Barred Spiral Galaxy, it belongs to the Fornax Cluster of galaxies and is an unusually clean example of a barred spiral.
The central bar of NGC 1365 affects star formation throughout the whole galaxy. It also hides a supermassive black hole, concealed behind crowds of newly formed stars.

Barred spirals like NGC 1365 interest astronomers for more than their looks. Our own Milky Way is also a barred spiral, and because we cannot see it from outside, galaxies like NGC 1365, seen whole from outside, offer clues to how our home galaxy works.

understand.summary: The Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope observed NGC 1365 through g, r and i filters, covering visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.

explore: The image uses data from the Dark Energy Survey, which mapped hundreds of millions of galaxies with the Dark Energy Camera on Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope.

The 570-megapixel camera, one of the best-performing wide-field CCD imagers in the world, was designed for the survey, funded by the DOE and built and tested at Fermilab. The DOE and NSF operated it for the survey from 2013 to 2019. It now serves many other science programs.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a strong central bar, sweeping spiral arms and dark dust lanes.
